description:
This is the story that the news won't show you: One of the worst tornadoes in US history took place in El Reno, Oklahoma. In 2013, this monster tornado decimated multiple towns and left a devastating mark on the communities that will forever be impacted. 

Subscribe for more videos of nature's most dangerous disasters and the untold stories that they leave behind. 

Huge credit to TornadoTRX and HIGH RISK Chris for the video inspiration!

comments.text: I was caught in a tornado in my bronco where the TX and OK panhandles meet. I thought I was going to die too. It went from broad daylight to the blackest blackout you could imagine, the rain and the wind was so bad I could no longer see the road. The only way I could see the horizon was from lightning flashes. I'd try to make out the road based on those brief moments of visibility. At one point I stopped the Bronco and thought about turning around unsure of what to do, I reluctantly pressed on. I'm so glad I did because I later learned the tornado touched down and crossed over the highway right where I would've been right when I would've been driving back had I turned around. Never want to do that again!

comments.text: You are right the 2013 El Reno tornado is only a EF3 at most because the damage was quite weak compared to other violent EF4/EF5 tornadoes. And the wind speed measurement that recorded winds up 310+ mph is also quite unreliable for several reasons. First the wind speed of 310+ was recorded hundreds of feet above the ground in a sub Vortex which isn't very good evidence to justify this tornado being on par with any other violent level tornado that we have seen before and after 2013. 2nd point most violent tornadoes are not recorded by mobile Doppler radar, which means that the 2013 El Reno tornado is in a small sample of tornadoes that have actually been recorded with mobile doppler rader. Where's the one's in the April 27th super tornado outbreak were not recorded by mobile doppler rader. Which means we don't know how strong those tornadoes were in comparison to other tornadoes that have been recorded by mobile doppler rader.
